newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money easy on improved funds supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money easy on improved funds supply.

text.p: Indian call money ended Monday at 4.50-4.75 percent, off the day's opening quotes of 5.5-6.0 percent, on good funds supply, dealers said.
They said a net inflow of around 13 billion rupees to banks had improved liquidity and pushed call money rates down.

"The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) reversed last Wednesday's repo of 29 billion rupees while outflows towards Saturday's auction was only 16.05 billion," said a dealer at a private bank. "The net effect was an inflow which boosted liquidity."
Dealers said prices of government securities were firm with interest concentrated in select securities.

"The 12 percent government of India 1999 stock and treasury bill maturing on July 18 were actively traded today," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "A state-run bank was selling off treasury bills in big chunks and this led to a rise in yields."
He said the July 18 treasury bill traded on Monday at yields between 9.7 percent and 9.8 percent against its last traded 9.6 percent.
"Volumes traded in the July 18 bill were about 500 million rupees," the dealer said.
Treasury bills maturing in August yielded 9.9-9.95 percent and December bills 10.05-10.08 percent, dealers said.
The 12 percent 1999 stock traded on Monday between 99.92 rupees and 100.02 against its last traded 99.90, dealers said.
The 13.25 percent 1997 stock traded at 101.36 rupees against 101.31. The 13.50 percent 1997 traded at 101.40 rupees against buyers' quotes of 101.37 on Saturday, dealers said.
There were no trades in certificates of deposit or commercial paper, they said.
